speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you are pregnant and experiencing fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise. To help me determine the cause, how many weeks pregnant are you, and when did these symptoms first begin?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old female at 30 weeks gestation. The patient presents with a sudden onset of fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise. She reports the consumption of ice cream 3 days prior to the onset of symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. The sudden onset of fever, headache, anorexia, and fatigue at 30 weeks gestation is concerning; did you experience a severe headache behind the eyes, vision changes, or swelling in your hands and face? Also, please confirm if you have had any similar symptoms before.

REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP, Urinalysis
REQUEST IMAGES: Fundoscopy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COMPLETE_BLOOD_COUNT: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL, Platelets 200,000 /μL; COMPREHENSIVE_METABOLIC_PANEL: AST Within normal limits, ALT Within normal limits, Bilirubin Within normal limits; URINALYSIS: Appearance Clear, WBC 0-5 /HPF, RBC 0-2 /HPF, Protein Negative, Glucose Negative; BLOOD_CULTURES: Gram-positive rods that are catalase-positive and show distinctive tumbling motility in the liquid medium.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Listeriosis (Listeria monocytogenes infection)

The blood culture showing Gram-positive rods with tumbling motility is pathognomonic for *Listeria monocytogenes*, which explains your sudden fever, headache, and anorexia at 30 weeks gestation. I am glad your liver enzymes and platelets are currently normal; please remain hospitalized immediately for IV ampicillin treatment to protect both you and the fetus.
